beats.text: How does one hand lift a two-tonne car?
Push on a sealed fluid, and the pressure spreads everywhere, equally.
Pressure is force, divided by area.
So on a piston a hundred times bigger, the same pressure makes a hundred times the force.
Twenty kilos of push. Two tonnes of lift.
The catch? The small piston moves a hundred times farther.
So a jack just pumps, a millimetre at a time. That's hydraulics.
Which machine should we break down next?
